body:
Founder asked whether we have a cron pulling observations into the kanban board on a schedule. Checked live, real process state rather than assuming: (1) cmd/observation-watcher is running continuously right now (PIDs 1265/1516, --root PRRJECT_FATBABY --prime-tasks EMILY/signals/tasks) and picks up a new emily observe within ~10s. (2) emily-agent --daemon (PID 1780) is genuinely alive and mid-cycle -- Apple #17234 'Cycle 12458 -- idle' filed 9 minutes before this check, proving its internal 15-min RSI cron (OBSERVE/DECIDE/ACT/PLAN, per EMILY/CLAUDE.md) is actively running, not stalled. The PLAN phase is what triages queued FatBaby observations into BACKLOG.md. (3) IDUNA's kanban Inbox (/admin/kanban/api/inbox, shipped this session as S234-01/02) reads BACKLOG.md's live unchecked items on every page load -- a pull, not a poll, so there's no scheduling gap on that leg either. End to end: observe -> (watcher, ~10s) -> directed task OR (daemon cron, ~15min) -> BACKLOG.md -> (kanban inbox, on-demand) -> visible on the board. This is a real, working, currently-running pipeline, just shaped as a long-running daemon + pull-based read rather than a literal cron job, which is why it wasn't obviously recognizable as 'a cron' at a glance. One stale artifact found along the way, noted but not acted on: EMILY/var/rsi-loop-state.json still shows iteration 177 / 2026-06-13 -- looks abandoned/superseded by whatever internal counter produced 'Cycle 12458', not something to fix without more signal that anything still reads it.

⚓ ☃
title: Confirmed: observations-into-kanban pipeline already exists, no new cron needed
